name: Prize crossword No 22,225
preamble: Method: Solve the clue and fit the solutions into the diagram jigsaw-wise, wherever they will go.

clue.text: As 2 to 4, free home holds roe or stew

indicators.note: to stew is to cook things together until they lose shape, so the preceding letters get jumbled
something that holds has other material sitting inside it, wrapped round by its letters

blocks.note: a squat is a dwelling occupied without paying rent
taken as written, ready for mixing

explanation.surface: An odd recipe: a free house holding fish roe or a stew, with a sum about two and four.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled ROE OR goes inside SQUAT to give SQUAREROOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Two multiplied by itself makes four, so two stands in that relation to four: it is its square root.

clue.text: We hear it locked: it’s where we may have docked

indicators.note: hearing points to the sound of the word rather than its spelling

blocks.note: the thing that locked a door is a key, said aloud the same as a landing place

explanation.surface: A rhyming couplet about hearing a lock click and arriving at a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A quay is a stone wharf where boats tie up, so it is where a ship has berthed.

clue.text: No thought required to fall upstairs, it’s said

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so we work from how the words sound out loud

blocks.note: fall is the American word for autumn, and the room upstairs under the roof is the attic

explanation.surface: Tripping up the stairs, it is claimed, happens without thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall upstairs' looks like a stumble on a staircase, but it is a season plus a room; run together, they make a word for reflex action.
explanation.definitionFit: An action done without conscious reflection, by reflex or habit, is called automatic.

clue.text: To last at last, translate translated street

indicators.note: to translate is to carry across into another form, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: at last means in the end
street rendered into French is rue

explanation.surface: A wordplay-heavy instruction about finally turning a street name into another language.
explanation.walkthrough: Translation works twice here: once into French for the street, once more to reshuffle that French word.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to survive or continue over time, which is what lasting means.

clue.text: Fly? No, they won’t - scraps from the kitchen scene

blocks.note: first meaning: the saying about something impossible, missing its final verb
second meaning: leftover food fed to farm animals
surface padding that sets the scene of a kitchen

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'pigs will fly' means it will never happen; the clue quotes the verb and leaves the first two words for you. The whole phrase also names leftover food for hogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigswill is kitchen waste given to hogs as feed, and the idiom ending 'fly' mocks hopeless expectation.

clue.text: Body-mind guy spoils Gothic boy that’s shocked

indicators.note: a shocked thing is jolted out of its normal state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A man ruins a goth teenager who is thoroughly startled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' looks like the verb of the sentence, but it is part of the material to be mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: This scientist studies how biology and behaviour link, so a person working on body and mind together.

clue.text: News for first friend is given in style that cheers

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
I is the Roman numeral one
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Good news for a best friend is delivered in a cheerful manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting genially means behaving in a warm, friendly, pleasant way that lifts people's mood.

clue.text: I leave the serviceman that runs at gate

indicators.note: the letter I walking out means it is removed from the word that follows

blocks.note: a waiter is a man who serves at table

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a soldier who is fleeing at the gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serviceman' suggests the armed forces, but here the service is at table.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid flows through a sluice or lock gate, so it is the stuff running at such a gate.

clue.text: Motion came through it - routine a la mode

indicators.note: a mode is a fashion or manner, so the letters are made up in a new fashion

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A proposal at a meeting passed by a fashionable routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Motion here is Andrew Motion, Britain's Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009, not a proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: Laureation is the act of crowning someone with laurels, the honour by which a poet becomes laureate.

clue.text: It’s never, never French - heard Sloan’s inburst

indicators.note: heard tells us to use the sound of the French word, not its spelling
something bursting in forces its way inside another piece

blocks.note: French for never, written as it sounds
Tod Sloan was an American jockey whose name gave the slang 'on your tod', meaning alone

explanation.surface: A garbled mix of a French word and some bloke called Sloan bursting in.
explanation.walkthrough: In Through the Looking-Glass the White Queen's rule is jam tomorrow and jam yesterday, but never jam today.
explanation.definitionFit: From Lewis Carroll, the phrase stands for a promised reward that never actually arrives.

clue.text: So far so good; but, with appeal dismissed, Love’s footman Allen, alien, seen on screen

annotation.answer: NOT OUT OF THE WOODY ET

blocks.note: in cricket, when the fielders' appeal is turned down the batsman is not out
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
split as foot, abbreviated FT, plus man, the pronoun HE
Woody Allen, the film director
E.T. is the alien of Spielberg's film

explanation.surface: A rambling cricket-and-cinema scene of a footman, a film director and a space visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Footman' looks like a servant but splits into foot and man.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says danger or difficulty has not passed yet, though things have gone well up to now.

clue.text: Hawk Spooner’s cruel registrar or priest

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of pairs of words

blocks.note: cruel is harsh, and a registrar or priest is one who conducts weddings

explanation.surface: An unkind wedding official who drives a hard bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: This bird of prey hunts low over reedbeds and wetlands; it belongs to the raptor family.

clue.text: Where Roman pipes were furred, loon went awry

definitions.note: an adjective or adverb of place; the phrase describes the location

indicators.note: things that went awry went wrong, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Old Roman plumbing got clogged and a crazy fellow went off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: Romans heated villas by a hypocaust, with hot air running in channels beneath the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Heating ducts beneath a room are under the floor, exactly where the Roman hypocaust carried warm air.

clue.text: A sandpiper at speed with bond or node

blocks.note: first meaning: a small wading bird
also a unit of speed at sea, one nautical mile per hour
second meaning: a tie in rope, or a lump or joint in wood

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings are packed in: a bird, a measure of speed at sea, and a tie or lump.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a wading shorebird, a fastening made by tying rope, and a hard joint in timber.

clue.text: On church roof lovely lady keeps a bed

definitions.note: the answer is a noun; this phrase says where it is

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A beauty sleeps up on the church roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lovely lady' could be any beauty, but the crossword favourite is the French-derived belle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellcote is a small gabled shelter on a church roof that houses one or more bells.

clue.text: Way up on wheels to junction on Scots rail

blocks.note: wheels is slang for a car
stairs are a way to go up

explanation.surface: Driving up a road to a Scottish railway junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the way up on top of the wheels, so the car comes first. Carstairs is a well-known railway junction in Lanarkshire, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The place is the junction where the West Coast Main Line divides for Glasgow and Edinburgh in Scotland.

clue.text: 3rd 2 prepared in Wiltshire for tattoo

definitions.note: a place name described by location and event

indicators.note: prepared means made ready by working on, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the figures spelt out as words

explanation.surface: A cryptic military instruction to get something ready in Wiltshire for a display.
explanation.walkthrough: '3rd 2' looks like a cross-reference to the third word of another clue, but the figures are simply spelt out. Tidworth is an army town in Wiltshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: This garrison town in Wiltshire hosted the Tidworth Tattoo, a military display of music and drill.

clue.text: A Roman coin, last City feature, round

definitions.note: the coin was Venetian, Italian rather than strictly Roman

blocks.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
EC is the postcode of the City of London
the chin is a facial feature
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Some old coin was the final feature of a city tour.
explanation.definitionFit: The zecchino was a gold coin struck in Venice and used across Italy for centuries.

clue.text: See 1
Allen again? Kiss idly, love not straight

definitions.note: a cryptic hint: a word meaning woody

indicators.note: letters that are not straight are bent out of their usual line

blocks.note: X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Woody Allen again, kissing lazily and loving crookedly.
explanation.walkthrough: The earlier clue used Allen for Woody; here the Allen hint asks for a word that means woody.
explanation.definitionFit: Xyloid is a technical adjective meaning resembling or made of wood, so it is a learned synonym for woody.

clue.text: See 10
To cover stake a barrier, X, appears

blocks.note: first meaning: to protect a bet by betting the other way too
second meaning: a row of bushes forming a boundary
surface padding; X marks the barrier as though on a map

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stake' could be a fence post, which fits a barrier, but here it is a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamblers offset risk by placing a counter-bet, and a line of shrubs fences off a field.

clue.text: Between the hills the Romans said goodbye

blocks.note: first meaning: a valley
second meaning: the Latin word of farewell

explanation.surface: Romans bidding farewell in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names low ground lying in a valley, and Latin speakers used it for farewell.

clue.text: In Thorganby on Derwent there is found

indicators.note: in tells us the letters lie inside the run of place names

blocks.note: inside thorganbY ON DERwent

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire village on the River Derwent and what can be found there.
explanation.walkthrough: Thorganby is a village in North Yorkshire on the River Derwent.
explanation.definitionFit: This old adverb means over there, at a distance, so it serves for there.

clue.text: When Fate plays tricks, press turns lac insect first

definitions.note: an adverbial clause describing what is ironical, which is an adjective

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word before it
something that turns faces the other way, read from the back

blocks.note: to iron clothes is to press them
the first letter of insect
lac is the resin secreted by an insect

explanation.surface: Destiny mocks us while a printing press churns out lac insect material.
explanation.walkthrough: Lac is a resin made by a scale insect; 'insect first' asks only for its initial, which goes before the turned lac.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironical outcome is one where fate mocks expectation, producing the opposite of what was meant.

clue.text: It’s Weber’s hunter sounding cold with heat

indicators.note: sounding points to how the words come out when spoken

blocks.note: cold is freeze, heat is hot

explanation.surface: A huntsman from a German opera somehow chilly and hot at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Weber's opera Der Freischütz is often translated The Marksman; its title is literally free-shot.
explanation.definitionFit: The German title word for the opera's marksman translates literally as a free shot, the hunter of the story.

clue.text: Performed with lady in, was made to fail

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: did means performed
she is the pronoun for a lady

explanation.surface: A performance with a woman involved ended in failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady' is often SHE in crosswords; 'performed' is the past tense, so the verb did.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dished is informal British for being ruined or defeated, one's hopes spoiled.
